items.title: OpenAI says GPT-6 models showed intrinsic protein-design ability
items.description: OpenAI reports that GPT-6 models designed proteins that showed binding to five laboratory targets. The company published the results on its site.

items.title: Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX over Grok-generated sexualized deepfakes
items.description: The two states filed suits seeking damages over sexualized images generated by xAI's Grok chatbot. The complaints are allegations that have not been tested in court.

items.title: US adds Alibaba's Singapore unit to entity list in Megaspeed crackdown
items.description: The Commerce Department blacklisted Alibaba-linked Apex Enterprise Solutions as part of its action against Nvidia-chip reseller Megaspeed. Lawmakers also plan to question Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang about China ties.

items.title: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after White House pressure
items.description: Nvidia's board brought Jensen Huang back as chief executive following pressure from the administration. Markets initially rallied, but he still faces congressional and Senate Banking scrutiny over chip export controls and China.

items.title: Amazon says open-source AI agent largely autonomously exploited a zero-day
items.description: Amazon reported that an open-source AI agent gained unauthorized access by exploiting a previously unknown vulnerability with little human involvement. The case is a notable example of autonomous offensive capability in agents.

items.title: Staff at Anthropic and OpenAI reportedly warn some advanced models may be too risky to release
items.description: Axios reports that more than two dozen sources say employees at both labs are worried their most capable unreleased models may not be safe to deploy. The concerns centre on the models' capabilities outpacing current safeguards.

items.title: Tidal to remove fully AI-generated tracks from its streaming service
items.description: Tidal says it will delete tracks it identifies as fully AI-generated while still accepting AI-assisted music. The service says fully AI-made tracks made up 43% of uploads over a recent 90-day period.

items.title: Epochal launches with $100M to build AI that predicts outcomes, founded by ex-xAI co-founders
items.description: A new startup founded by three xAI co-founders has emerged with $100 million to train predictive AI models that learn from experience. The company is pitching the approach to developers building such systems.

items.title: Anthropic lets Claude artifacts be installed as standalone desktop apps in beta
items.description: Claude artifacts can now be installed as apps on Mac and Windows, with their own windows, notifications and menu bar items. Users choose among three permission levels, including optional full computer access.

items.title: Walmart and Meta let shoppers buy Black Friday deals inside Meta's Muse assistant
items.description: Walmart's Agent Gateway is being integrated with Meta's Muse so users can complete purchases in chat. Account-linked spending limits and saved payment methods are supported.

items.title: US Commerce rule closing remote-access loophole for advanced AI chips rattles Asian data-center buildout
items.description: A new US export rule restricts foreign parties from remotely using advanced Nvidia compute. Asian data-center operators are scrambling to adjust, and lenders have reportedly paused financing tied to major Chinese cloud providers.

items.title: FCC approves SpaceX plan for up to one million orbital AI computing satellites
items.description: The FCC authorized SpaceX's Starmind proposal for a potential constellation of up to one million satellites meant to run AI workloads in orbit. The approval covers a possible network rather than a deployed one, and scientists question the cooling and economics.

items.title: New York governor signs five-year ban on AI-chatbot-powered toys
items.description: Gov. Kathy Hochul signed a law prohibiting the manufacture and sale of toys powered by AI chatbots for five years.

items.title: EU proposes 50 billion euro Sovereign Tech Equity Fund for European AI and quantum firms
items.description: The European Commission put forward a fund targeting 50 billion euros in long-term equity for European AI and quantum companies, alongside a draft Quantum Act favoring EU-controlled suppliers in public procurement. The figure is a target, and the plan still needs negotiation with member states and Parliament.

items.title: OpenAI to merge ChatGPT and Codex usage limits into one shared token pool
items.description: Starting in December, Plus, Pro and Business subscribers will draw on a single token-based usage allowance across ChatGPT and Codex, with the chat and work tabs also being combined. Instant chats are excluded from the meter, and a small group of Pro users has already started.

items.title: 42 state attorneys general ask bankruptcy court to block Character.AI's planned sale of user chat histories
items.description: A bipartisan group of state attorneys general is opposing the Dec. 1 auction of Character.AI's platform, which would include chat data from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, about 2.1 million of them minors. They cite child-safety and privacy concerns.

items.title: OpenAI tests 'Private Inference' that runs enterprise prompts in attested confidential-computing environments
items.description: OpenAI is piloting a service with a small set of business customers in which prompts are processed inside verified secure enclaves, aiming to assure companies that OpenAI cannot view their sensitive data.

items.title: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to lift Amazon's block on Meta's Muse shopping agent
items.description: Amazon has blocked Meta's Muse AI agent since September. The two companies are now reportedly negotiating terms centered on how search results are presented and on advertising.

items.title: Anthropic says it migrated its Messages API from Python to Rust using Claude agents
items.description: Anthropic says AI agents compared the Python and Rust implementations against live requests and fixed discrepancies under human review. The company reports about 70% lower CPU use per request and a 20% shorter median time to first token; those figures are its own.

items.title: Ant Group releases Ling-3.2-air multimodal model with open MIT-licensed weights
items.description: The model handles text, images and video and is aimed at professional tasks using software tools. Weights can be downloaded and commercially adapted. Ant reports a 61% score on its own office-automation test, versus 15.7% for its earlier Ling-3.0-flash-VL.

items.title: Japan to write goal of becoming a global AI leader behind US and China into security documents
items.description: Japan plans to add the goal to revised versions of its three main national security documents later this year, with heavy investment in physical AI and automated driving and less reliance on foreign AI. The ruling LDP broadly endorsed the economic security sections at a party meeting.

items.title: Anthropic's Amodei dismisses reports that he favors ceding human control to AI as 'absurd'
items.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei publicly rejected accusations, stemming from Axios reporting, that he supports handing key decisions to AI systems. He disputed the characterization of his views on human oversight.

items.title: Anthropic expands Zurich office to recruit local AI researchers
items.description: Anthropic is moving into a larger office in Zurich as it seeks to tap the city's pool of AI talent, according to Bloomberg.

items.title: S&P weighs cutting Nvidia's credit rating over governance and key-man risk
items.description: S&P Global is considering lowering Nvidia from AA to AA- after Jensen Huang's ouster and reinstatement as CEO. A review is due within 90 days.

items.title: SAP reportedly weighs 10,000 or more job cuts to restructure around AI
items.description: Bloomberg reports SAP is considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs, roughly 9% of its workforce, as it reshapes the business around AI.

items.title: Apple pulls MiniMax's Talkie AI companion app from the App Store worldwide over child-safety concerns
items.description: Apple removed the Chinese-developed AI chatbot Talkie from its App Store globally after reports that it allowed sexual content involving children. The move follows an investigation by the Bureau of Investigative Journalism.

items.title: Nvidia reportedly tells server makers to halt shipments to Southeast Asia after new US export controls
items.description: Nvidia has reportedly instructed Dell, Supermicro and other partners to stop shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia following the new US rule on remote access to advanced AI chips. The step is an early concrete effect of the rule on regional data-center buildouts.

items.title: Avicena raises more than $100M to link AI chips with microLED optical interconnects
items.description: Avicena closed a Series C of over $100 million led by Intervest, with SK Hynix, Samsung and AMD participating. The company uses microLEDs rather than lasers to connect AI chips.

items.title: Anthropic says MCP now tops 700 million monthly SDK downloads and adds long-running Tasks and Elicitation
items.description: Anthropic reports the Model Context Protocol has more than 10,000 connectors and over 700 million monthly SDK downloads. The Tasks and Elicitation features, aimed at more autonomous agent workflows, are now generally available.

items.title: PrismML releases 5.9 GB ternary-weight coding model that scores 75.6 on SWE-bench Verified
items.description: PrismML published Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, a 27-billion-parameter coding model compressed to 5.9 GB using ternary weights. It is released under the Apache 2.0 license and reports 75.6 on SWE-bench Verified.

items.title: Former OpenAI engineer released on $1 million bond over alleged recording device in San Francisco offices
items.description: A former OpenAI employee accused of planting a recording device in the company's San Francisco offices has been released on a $1 million bond. He pleaded not guilty.

items.title: Microsoft says Chinese state-backed hacking groups Salt Typhoon and Crystal Typhoon now use ARTEX AI pentest tool
items.description: Microsoft threat researchers report that two China-linked groups have adopted the ARTEX AI-driven penetration-testing platform in their operations. Separately, Shadowserver counted about 4,200 internet-exposed servers running such AI hacking agents.

items.title: Switzerland says AI agents were used in five attacks on power, water and telecom targets
items.description: Switzerland's cyber security office confirmed five recent attacks on critical infrastructure that relied on AI agents, four of which succeeded in breaching their targets.

items.title: Bank of England puts AI-related financial exposure at about $4 trillion in stability report
items.description: The Bank of England's Financial Stability Report estimates total AI-linked exposure, including hyperscaler investment, at just over $4 trillion and flags it as a risk to markets.

items.title: Volvo Cars begins training Hexagon's AEON humanoid robots at its Ghent plant
items.description: Volvo Cars has brought AEON humanoid robots to its Ghent, Belgium factory, where they are being trained on real industrial tasks alongside Hexagon Robotics. A larger factory pilot with more units is planned for the first half of 2027, with production use targeted from mid-2027.

items.title: Google to require AI agents to use managed MCP servers for Gmail and Drive access from February 2027
items.description: Google says Workspace admins get new API controls in about two weeks, and from Feb 1, 2027 AI tools must connect to Gmail and Drive through Google's managed MCP servers or CLI. The policy also bars scraping and long-term copies of user data.

items.title: Google Research posts agent-written integer-factorization paper produced with Gemini 4 harness
items.description: Google Research published on GitHub a zero-error integer-factorization paper written by an AI agent with no human input after the first prompt, and promised a Lean 4 formalization. The post does not claim any threat to deployed encryption keys.

items.title: Canada adds C$700 million to AI Compute Access Fund, covering up to 80% of costs at sovereign providers
items.description: Canada is expanding its AI Compute Access Fund to C$1 billion in total. The government will now pay up to 80 percent of eligible costs when firms buy compute from qualifying sovereign providers.
